name: wolf
author: logic-agent
description: PRIVATE. Elementary cellular automaton rule induction (name: Wolfram). Clue = 4-6 'before>after' pairs of equal-length binary strings (length 10-14), where after = one synchronous step of a hidden rule 0..255 with WRAP-AROUND (cell i sees i-1, i, i+1 mod L). Solution = the 8-bit rule as a binary string, MSB first: s[7-p] is the new state for neighbourhood p read as a 3-bit number, i.e. exactly format(rule,'08b') in the standard Wolfram numbering. Any rule consistent with all pairs scores 1, and unobserved neighbourhoods leave several rules valid - deliberate slack. DIFFICULTY: hard. DISCOVERY PATH: the demo is the whole lesson - the clue is pairs of equal-length bit strings, the answer is exactly 8 bits, and 8 = 2^3 is the tell that each cell depends on three neighbours. Gradient: a random 8-bit answer scores 1/256 by luck, but once a team fits ANY local window rule they get near 100%; scanning all 256 rules against the pairs takes microseconds. The wrap-around is the classic trap: interior right + two ends wrong scores 0, a strong findable hint from a single failing attempt.
